Porch: Photorealistic-natural. Make one finished vertical 4:5 photographic print, full bleed, an ordinary family snapshot circa 1958 on the timber porch of a modest rural American farmhouse. Four fictional people ONLY: Edith Harrow, husband Walter, son Danny (about 10), daughter Ruth (about 5). The attached still is a casting reference: Edith is the younger, healthy, happy version of the elderly white-haired woman at far right, now chestnut-brown softly waved hair pinned back, high cheekbones, kindly creased eyes and an expressive smile; use the man at far left as Walter, deep-set eyes, dark side-parted hair, lean and clean-shaven. Match the two children to the boy and little girl in the still. Do not include the extra adult woman or any supernatural elements. Edith and Walter lean shoulder-to-shoulder behind the kids; Ruth has just giggled, Danny and both parents are smiling naturally at the family friend taking the picture. Period cotton blouse and everyday shirts, gingham, realistic teeth, subtly uneven focus in warm daylight, beautiful but ordinary people. Faces form a compact group in the middle 65% of the print, plenty of headroom, portrait/oval crop safe. Authentic slightly faded midcentury color film, clear eyes and readable faces, soft grain. The whole image is the photograph itself. No text, watermark, border, damage, horror, additional figures, ornament, collage or physical frame.

Faded warm color flash print.

Daniel.direction: Only Danny, the boy at lower left in the reference, age-progressed to nineteen, just before 1969. All four faces smiling, natural imperfect flash, a few blurred Christmas lights at the edge. All four faces fit in the central 70%; this is a portrait photograph suitable for a tall frame.

VowsDefaced.decay: Edit the reference photograph. Identity, composition, posing, gaze and especially the friendly genuine smiling expressions must be kept EXACTLY as in this particular snapshot. Recreate it as an eerie almost completely GREYSCALE silver-gelatin print: cold gray whites, graphite midtones, slightly faded corners, visible midtones, no brown/sepia or color. The photographic paper and glass are intact. Within the picture the subjects' SKIN itself has become disturbingly, unambiguously decayed in a dry mummified way: asymmetrical graphite-black mottling beneath the skin, large islands of pale grey peeling skin, fine wrinkled parchment stretched over the cheeks and temples, slightly sunken sockets. The decay follows facial contours, visible also on the hands. The clothes and background are still ordinary. Keep human eyes looking through their sockets, keep the teeth and the special geometry of each old smile identical. They are still smiling for the camera like it is a normal, happy day. Make the decay legible across a room and at thumbnail size. Real analog photography. No liquid, blood, exposed muscle or bone, missing body parts, grotesque wide grins, blacked-out mouths, horns, extra figures, clawed shadows, scratches across the print or labels. Vertical 4:5 edge-to-edge. The two adults, Edith and Walter still smile naturally with visibly decaying gray cheeks and foreheads.

Old photographic paper, full bleed portrait, no text, color tint, other surface scratches, blood, or bodily injury. Viewer sees the damaged print, not a physical frame.
